title: What Dutre knows of his father's life and death
summary: He recalls his father came to New Orleans, ran a pressing shop, worked as a barber and played with various outfits; died about 1941.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Yes, I understand. I wonder if you could give us a little information about your father, if you remember how old he was and when he died, so we can figure out just about his birth date. Do you remember when he was born or any of the facts about his life that way?

Well, I couldn't say too much about that because we never could voice on that. But from what I heard, he first came to New Orleans and bought him a pressing shop. And after which he went to the barber. And he began playing music with different outfits in New Orleans.
He worked as the barber in the press?
In a presser. That's been quite a while back then.

Yes, certainly I understand. When you were a kid, you weren't interested in all those things, so you wouldn't be interested in trying to remember it at that time. And now, of course, we're interested in all that oldest history that we can find about the musicians because the whole world, as you know, considers it important now. I wonder, do you remember the date of his death?

I had some notes here I'd gotten from somebody that I don't know if they were accurate. It said 1941. Do you think that would be right at the beginning of the war? Can you remember? Just about the time.
It's about 1941. We got into the war.
We got into, you know, Pearl Harbor. It was 1941, December.
It was 40 or 41. About that time.
Do you remember how old he was?
